Results.ReviewText:
As someone who never cooks, I was worried I'd spend all this money on the Q1200 and cart and use it once. (My previous grill was a monster that I used 3 times in 20 years.) But I love it and am using it several times a week. In fact, I just made a Portobello mushroom cap "burger" on a toasted bun for lunch!  

The Q1200's just a super, compact and convenient grill that takes up little space on my deck. It feels lighter than I expected -- most of the weight is in the grates. The flip-out shelves are an awesome convenience. The grill temperature easily climbs to it's maximum -- you have to keep an eye on it. The grilling surface is large enough to easily handle a large cut up chicken, and cooks quickly.  (I've had an easier time cooking chicken to juicy perfection on this Q1200 than I do when using an oven, especially the large split breasts.)  Depending on what you're cooking, you could easily feed 6-8 people with this grill -- probably even more. 

Even though the cooking surface is smaller than a regular size grill, it's comprised of two separate grates, which makes them easy to handle and transport as they're heavy. (I often just use one side which minimizes the number of grates I have to clean.)  Of course, the split surface also provides the option to switch out one side for a griddle plate. (I bought the plate, but have yet to try it.)  It's also notable that the grill grates are broad with less space in between, which means you can throw some fairly small things on there without food falling through.

I initially used the small 1lb propane bottles as I wasn't sure how much I'd grill (I otherwise NEVER cook); but I've been using the Q1200 so much that I transitioned to a regular propane tank. It was very easy to set it up with the adapter hose and the propane tank. Fortunately, I was aware that using a tank can trigger a safety mechanism that prevents the grill from fully heating. There are helpful instructions on the Weber website on how to prevent that so I've had no issues. 

The Q1200's been pretty easy to clean, but I'm diligent about cleaning after every use. Burning everything off with high heat, and then using a grill brush is a FALLACY though. The Weber Grill Grate cleaner helps quite a bit with degreasing and the removal of charred buts. I also spray on liquid detergent and let the grates sit in the sink a few minutes. Again, it's wonderful having compact grates when it comes to cleaning.

I highly recommend getting the rolling cart designed for the Q series. It's lightweight but sufficiently stable, and puts the grill at the perfect height. (However, I have not tried transporting the grill and cart anywhere to test their mobility.)

Seriously, I can't recommend this enough

ClientResponses.Response:
We appreciate your feedback. We are so sorry to hear your Q1200 is not getting hot. We are happy to help. 

If you are using your grill with the adapter hose to a larger 20 lb. refill/exchange LP tank, it sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. Follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is also the way you would want to start your grill each and every time.
 
Open the lid
Make sure the control knob is in the off position
Turn your LP tank on all the way
Wait 60 seconds
Turn the burner to start/high (first position to the left)
Hit your igniter
Close the lid to preheat to 500-550°F
 
For troubleshooting purposes, I would suggest using your grill with a 14 or 16 oz. disposable LP cylinder as well. That will let you know right away if the issue is with the grill, or with the adapter hose/LP tank.

Our Care team is reaching out to assist you further. Please look for our outreach soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText: This is my third Weber grill and my first Weber tabletop model.  I recently purchased the Q1200 to replace a different brand as my new RV grill. I BBQed on three separate nights: salmon, ribeye and chicken thighs.  The unit operated as it should.  There was a learning curve to place the meat on the grill at the correct temperature as not to have the burner flame up and burn the meat.  The grates are heavy and retain the heat so from my experience, reducing the flame to low doesn't immediately lower the cooking temp.  The grill preheated to 500 degrees at highest setting and I had to lower the setting after placing the meat on the grill.  On my third use only preheated to 375, no flame up.  The cooking grill is in two haves and is easy to clean in the sink after use.  I prefer to have a temp gauge on my BBQs, one of the reasons I selected this model.  I am planning on cooking a whole chicken as a friend recommended.  He stated it possible due to the dome style hood design.  The folding side tables are handy but for my use there not really needed.  Overall, I would recommend this grill to cook for 1 to 4 persons.
Results.Title: My third Weber grill
